page.layout: One block of verse lines in the centre of the page; running head at the top; catchword at the lower right, cut off. Ragged marginal stains on the right edge, not text.

l.i: Nec thura, nec molas, nec hostias cremat.
Iam saepe frustra illum adortus, nam meis
Sic crebro ariete pulsa tandem moenia
Fouet quidem Abramum Deus, atque pluribus
Hunc secum amico iunxit: at Deus sua
Si dicta mutet, ecce mox ruet miser.
Abramus: illi nil fides, nec Sinuida
Prodesse quicquam spes poterit, ni manserit
Idem per omne tempus, Ꝯ immotus Sebut
Rupes medio aequore quam procella Ꝯerberat.
Duos habet ecce liberos, alter meus
Iam paret Ꝯltro nutibus: Ꝯix retia
Imbellis iste sexus, Ꝯ constans parum.

page.notes: Some words in the final lines are doubtful because of the ragged edge and ink damage; the Greek-style ampersand-like marks (Ꝯ) are read as "&" / "et" abbreviations and are uncertain. The catchword at lower right is partly cut off and marked as "Versa" with doubt. The page number is not printed.
